title: Triangulated closure of the actual uniform integral finite-Tor predicate
statement: For a prime l, a finite coefficient field stage E over Q_l, and a scheme T, the actual completed integral finite-Tor property finiteTorConstructibleIntegral(l,E.carrier,T) of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is triangulated. Thus for each K in this predicate and each r ∈ Z, K[r] is again in it, with a uniform interval for every positive finite reduction.

source.place: Tags 05SU, 06YU, 07A6, 0B56, 0941, 099I, 099L; retained canonical scalar-shift argument of lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-normalization.

proof.text: The completed constructible property is triangulated by the intrinsic integral-constructible theorem. For the uniform Tor property, every reduction has an exact derived scalar extension and hence a coherent shift. A shift r translates the common interval [a,b] to [a-r,b-r]; finite Tor shift invariance transports it through the reduction shift iso. For triangles take minimum lower and maximum upper endpoints and use the finite Tor triangle assertion. These intervals are independent of the reduction level. Intersect the two triangulated predicates. This is the already proved integralTriangulated helper in ConstructibleExceptionalAdjunctionCoefficientsData, without depending on the later exceptional-adjunction theorem.
